Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:11:1.hebrew: מכי משנה שכר שכיר נפקא - גמרינן בעל כרחו, וכי תנא ביה קרא אדוניו יתן לו כו', למעוטי מוכר עצמו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:11:1.english: He derives it from "For double the hire of a hired worker" - We learn [that he remains] against his will [from this verse]. And where the verse teaches about him, "His master shall give him..." etc., [this is] to exclude one who sold himself.

Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:14:1.hebrew: ושב אל משפחתו - במוכר עצמו כתיב, לומר שיצא ביובל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:14:1.english: And he shall return to his family - It is written regarding one who sold himself, to say that he goes out at the Jubilee.

Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:14:2.hebrew: אם במוכר עצמו - הכתוב מדבר, וללמד שאם פגעו יובל בתוך שש, יובל מוציאו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:14:2.english: If [it is speaking] of one who sold himself - [and the verse comes] to teach that if the Jubilee Year arrived within the six [years], the Jubilee frees him:

Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:14:3.hebrew: הרי כבר אמור - דכתיב לעיל מיניה: "עד שנת היובל יעבוד עמך":
Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:14:3.english: It is already stated - For it is written immediately above it: "Until the Jubilee Year he shall work with you."

Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:15:1.hebrew: אם בנרצע - ללמד שאף הנרצע יוצא ביובל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:15:1.english: If [it is speaking] of a pierced slave - To teach that even the pierced slave goes out in the Jubilee.

Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:15:2.hebrew: הרי כבר אמור - לקמיה בעי לה מאי היא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:15:2.english: Behold, it is already stated - Further on, [the Gemara] asks what it is.

Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:16:1.hebrew: דלא עבד איסורא - דלא גנב כלום. אבל מכרוהו ב"ד בגניבתו, אימא נימא נקנסיה לעבוד עד שש:
Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:16:1.english: Who did not commit a transgression - Who did not steal anything. But [one whom] the court sold for his theft, [one might say:] let us penalize him to serve until six [years].

Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:16:2.hebrew: ליקנסיה - על שאמר ״לא אצא״, ועבר על ״כי עבדי הם״ (ויקרא כ״ה:מ״ב), והוא קונה אדון לעצמו חנם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:16:2.english: Let us penalize him - Because he said, “I will not go out [free],” and transgressed [the verse] “For they are My servants” (Leviticus 25:42), and he acquires a master for himself for free.

Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:17:1.hebrew: ושבתם איש אל אחוזתו - בפרשת יובל כתיב:
Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:17:1.english: “And you shall return, each man to his land” - It is written in the section about the Jubilee Year.

Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:17:2.hebrew: הרי כבר אמור - כדאמר לעיל: ״עד שנת היובל יעבוד עמך״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:17:2.english: It is already stated - As it said above: "He shall labor with you until the Jubilee Year."

Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:18:1.hebrew: אי במכרוהו ב"ד הרי כבר אמור - הכתוב "ושב אל משפחתו", כדאוקימנא לעיל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:18:1.english: If [it speaks of one] whom the court sold, it is already stated - "And he shall return to his family," as we established above.

Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:19:1.hebrew: דלא מטא זימניה - לא מלאו שש שניו לצאת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:19:1.english: For his time had not come - His six years had not been completed for him to go out.

Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:19:2.hebrew: ליקנסיה - על שאמר ״לא אצא״, ועבר על ״כי עבדי הם״ (ויקרא כ״ה:מ״ב), והוא קונה אדון לעצמו חנם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:19:2.english: Let us penalize him - Because he said, "I will not go free," and transgressed [the verse] "For they are My servants" (Leviticus 25:42), and he acquires a master for himself for free.

Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:1:1.hebrew: ונאמר להלן אוזן - במצורע עני, שכל הפרשה לדרשה, שהרי נאמרה לעצמה במצורע עשיר והוכפלה. והכי אמרינן במנחות (דף י.):
Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:1:1.english: And it is stated there, “ear” - With regard to a poor leper, [for] the entire passage is [available] for exposition, since it was already stated on its own with regard to a wealthy leper, and was repeated. And so we say in [tractate] Menachot (page 10a):

Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:20:1.hebrew: משום דעבד ליה שש - קודם לכן, ואין רבו מפסיד בשילוחו. אבל מכרוהו ב"ד, שפגע בו יובל בתוך שש, אימא דלא נפסדיה לאדון, קמ"ל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:20:1.english: Because he served him six [years] - beforehand, and his master does not lose out through his release. But [in the case of one] whom the court sold, whom the Jubilee struck within the six [years], one might say that we should not cause the master a loss; therefore [the Torah] teaches us [that he goes free as well].

Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:21:1.hebrew: לעולם - ועבדו לעולם, והוא לעולמו של יובל, דטפי מהכי ליכא למימר, דהא כתיב קרא אחרינא "ושבתם איש" וגו', ואוקימנא בנרצע:
Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:21:1.english: Forever - "And he shall serve him forever," and this means for the "forever" of the Jubilee, for more than this it is impossible to say, since another verse is written: "And you shall return, each man" etc., and we established it as referring to a pierced slave.

Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:22:1.hebrew: ה"מ - דקאמר דיוצא נרצע ביובל ולא קודם לכן, היכא דלא עבד שש אחר רציעה. אבל היכא דעבד שש אחר רציעתו, אימא ניפוק בשש, דלא תהא רציעה חמורה מתחילת ממכרו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:22:1.english: This statement - [that] one who goes out, [i.e., a pierced slave,] goes out at the Jubilee and not before it, applies where he did not serve six years after the piercing. But where he served six years after his piercing, I might say that he should go out after six, [reasoning] that the piercing should not be more severe than the beginning of his sale:

Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:22:2.hebrew: קמ"ל לעולם - היינו מידי דחשוב עד לעולם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:22:2.english: It teaches us “forever” - That is, something that is reckoned as lasting until “forever.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:3:1.hebrew: ההוא [מאוזן] ומיעוטא נפקא לן - מדכתיב ״אזנו״, דמשמע אזנו של זה ולא של אחר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:3:1.english: That [derives from "ozen"], and the exclusion we derive - From the fact that it is written "his ear," which implies the ear of this one and not of another:

Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:3:2.hebrew: ולא אזנה - של אמה העבריה נרצעת. והא דכתיב (דברים טו) "ואף לאמתך תעשה כן" — אהענקה קאי, כדלקמן (קידושין דף יז:):
Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:3:2.english: And not her ear - [That is, the ear] of a Hebrew maidservant is [not] pierced. And as for that which is written (Deuteronomy 15), "And also to your maidservant you shall do likewise" — it refers to the giving of gifts [upon release], as [stated] later (Kiddushin 17b).

Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:4:1.hebrew: כשהוא עבד - מ"ואם יאמר העבד" נפקא, שאם לא אמר "אהבתי את אדוני... לא אצא חפשי" עד שיכלו שש שניו — אינו נרצע:
Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:4:1.english: When he is a slave - It is derived from "And if the slave shall say" (Exodus 21:5): that if he did not say "I love my master… I will not go out free" until his six years were completed, he is not pierced.

Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:5:1.hebrew: עבד העבד - דרשינן עבד עד שיאמר כשהוא עבד. והאי העבד נפקא ליה מה"א יתירא, למעוטי אמה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:5:1.english: Slave, “the slave” - [We derive from] “slave” that [he may say this] only while he is [still] a slave. And [the law of] “the slave” he derives from the superfluous letter heh, to exclude a maidservant:

Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:5:2.hebrew: לא דריש - דאורחא דקרא לאישתעי הכי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:5:2.english: He does not derive - For it is the way of the verse to speak in this manner.

Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:7:1.hebrew: ולא ליורשיו - אם לא הספיק להעניקו עד שמת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:7:1.english: And not to his heirs - If [the master] did not manage to give him the severance gift before [the slave] died.

Rashi on Kiddushin 15a:7:2.english: His labor - The wages for his labor.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 15a:12:1.hebrew: כי טוב לו עמך - ה"ר אברהם גריס: "כשכיר כתושב יהיה עמך" (ויקרא כ״ה:מ׳), דמהתם ילפינן בת"כ. אבל בספרי לא דריש מידי מ"כי טוב לו עמך", דאין זה צווי אלא סיפור דברים בעלמא:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 15a:12:1.english: "Because he fares well with you" - Rabbi Avraham reads: "As a hired worker, as a resident, he shall be with you" (Leviticus 25:40), for from there we derive [this] in the Torat Kohanim. But in the Sifrei, [the Sages] do not derive anything from "Because he fares well with you," since this is not a command but merely a narration of matters.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 15a:13:1.hebrew: ואידך אי מהתם ה"א ה"מ מדעתיה - אף על גב דמדעתו, היינו מ"ואם אדוניו יתן לו אשה", נפקא, מ"מ הוה אמינא דלהרצאת אדון קאתי:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 15a:13:1.english: "And the other [Sage]: If [it were derived] from there, I would have said this applies only with his consent" - Even though [the law of a Canaanite maidservant given] with his consent is derived from "If his master gives him a wife" (Exodus 21:4), nevertheless I would have said that [the word "to him"] comes to [teach a law] for the satisfaction of the master.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 15a:18:1.hebrew: איזהו דבר שנוהג באיש ואינו נוהג באשה - ואם תאמר: ואימא זו מכרוהו ב"ד, דלא שייך באשה, דכתיב (שמות כב): "בגניבתו" ולא בגניבתה? וי"ל: דמ"מ שם מכירה נוהגת באשה, אבל שם רציעה אינו נוהג באשה. [ותימה: דכיון דקרא לא משתמע אלא בנרצע, למאי איצטריך למימר "אי במכרוהו ב"ד הרי כבר אמור"?] ת"י:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 15a:18:1.english: What matter applies to a man and does not apply to a woman - And if you say: But say that this is [a slave] sold by the court, which does not apply to a woman, as it is written (Exodus 22): "for his theft," and not for her theft? And one can answer: that in any case, the term "sale" applies to a woman, but the term "piercing" does not apply to a woman. [And it is puzzling: since the verse is understood only as referring to a pierced slave, why was it necessary to say, "If it is of one sold by the court, it is already stated"?] Tosafot Yeshanim.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 15a:1:1.hebrew: ואידך לג"ש הוא דאתא - פי': וצריך שתהא מופנה משני צדדין, דאי אינה מופנה אלא מצד אחד, איכא מ"ד (בנדה דף כב:) דלמידין ומשיבין. ומאי משיבין? דאיכא למיפרך: מה למצורע, שכן טעון עץ ארז ואזוב ושני תולעת:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 15a:1:1.english: "And the other [Sage] — it comes for a verbal analogy" - Explanation: And it is necessary that [the word] be free [of any other use] from both sides, for if it is free only from one side, there is an opinion (Niddah 22b) that one derives [from it] but [the derivation] may be refuted. And what does "may be refuted" mean? That there is room to challenge: What [is true] of the leper is [because] he requires cedar wood, hyssop, and crimson wool.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 15a:3:1.hebrew: ההוא נפקא מאוזן, ומיעוטא נפקא לן - מדכתיב "אזנו", דמשמע אזנו של זה ולא של אחר:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 15a:3:1.english: That is derived from "ozen," and the exclusion we derive - from the fact that it is written "his ear," which implies the ear of this one and not of another.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 15a:9:1.hebrew: ואידך - פי' ת"ק: בעלמא נמי לא ס"ל כר' נתן. מכאן מדקדקין דאין הלכה כר' נתן, דהא ר"א ורבנן פליגי בדר' נתן, ור' אליעזר דשמותי הוא סבר כר' נתן, והלכה כרבנן. ועוד מדקדק ר"ת מהא דאמר לקמן פ' האומר (קידושין דף סט.) גבי אושפזיכניה דר' שמלאי, ממזירא הוה, א"ל: אי קדימתך טהרתינהו לבנך. ומפרש משום דא"ל: זיל גנוב ואיזדבן לעבד עברי, ואי מוכר עצמו רבו מוסר לו שפחה כנענית, למה ליה למימר זיל גנוב? ה"ל למימר: זיל זבון עצמך! אלא ש"מ דאין הלכה כר"א, דודאי מוכר עצמו אין רבו מוסר לו שפחה כנענית. וכי היכי דבהא לית הילכתא כוותיה, בהא דקאמר מעניקין לו נמי לית הילכתא כוותיה, אלא ודאי אין מעניקין לו כת"ק. ועוד ראיה מהא דאמר לקמן (קידושין דף טז:): הא מני תוטאי היא, דאמר לו ולא לבעל חובו — משמע דאין הלכה כוותיה. ור"ת ור"י פי' דהלכה כר' נתן, דהא גבי פלוגתא דאביי ורבא בפרק כל שעה (פסחים דף לא.) דאמר רבא מכאן ולהבא הוא גובה, אי אפשר לרבא ליישב אליבא דרב נחמן — דאמר יתומים שגבו קרקע בחובת אביהן, בעל חוב חוזר וגובה אותה מהן — אלא כר' נתן. וקי"ל כרב נחמן בדיני, ורבא נמי דחק להעמידה כמותו, וקי"ל כרבא גבי אביי. ומה שהבאתי דמדלית הילכתא כר"א בהא דרבו מוסר לו שפחה כנענית, ה"נ נימא דלית הילכתא כוותיה בההיא דמעניקין לו — אין זה ראיה, דילמא בההיא אין הלכה כמותו, אבל באחריני הלכתא כוותיה. ועוד דשמא גם בהא דמוכר עצמו רבו מוסר לו שפחה כנענית נמי הילכתא כוותיה, והא דנקט התם זיל גנוב, לרווחא דמילתא נקט; דמכרוהו ב"ד כ"ע מודו דרבו מוסר לו שפחה כנענית. ומה שאומר דר"א שמותי הוא — ברוב ספרים גרס ר' אלעזר. והא דקאמר תוטאי היא — דילמא הכי קאמר: תוטאי היא, וס"ל כוותיה. וה"ר נתנאל מפרש: לגבי מלוה כ"ע אית להו כר' נתן, והכי נפרש לעיל אליבא דר"א: אלא לו ולא לבעל חובו — משום דסבירא לן בעלמא כר' נתן בשאר שכירות, שמוציאין מזה ונותנין לזה; אתא לו ואפקיה. פי' שאינו משלם הענקה לב"ח. ואידך ת"ק בעלמא נמי, פי' בשאר שכירות לא קי"ל כר' נתן, משום דטרח בגופו; אבל בב"ח כ"ע אית להו דרבי נתן, כדפי':
Tosafot on Kiddushin 15a:9:1.english: “And the other” - Explanation: The first *tanna* too does not hold like Rabbi Natan in general. From here they derive that the halakha is not like Rabbi Natan, for Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis disagree about Rabbi Natan, and Rabbi Eliezer, who is of the Shammaite school, holds like Rabbi Natan, and the halakha is like the Rabbis. Furthermore, Rabbeinu Tam derives this from what is stated later, in the chapter “HaOmer” (Kiddushin 69a), concerning the host of Rabbi Shmelai, who was a *mamzer*. [Rabbi Shmelai] said to him: “Had I come before you, I would have purified your sons.” And [the Gemara] explains: because he said to him, “Go steal and be sold as a Hebrew slave.” But if one who sells himself has his master give him a Canaanite maidservant, why did he need to say, “Go steal”? He should have said, “Go sell yourself!” Rather, learn from this that the halakha is not like Rabbi Eliezer, for certainly the master of one who sells himself does not give him a Canaanite maidservant. And just as the halakha is not like him on that point, so too on the point where he says that one gives him a severance gift, the halakha is not like him; rather, certainly one does not give him a severance gift, like the first *tanna*. And there is further proof from what is stated later (Kiddushin 16b): “Whose view is this? It is Tutai’s, who said ‘to him, and not to his creditor’” — which implies that the halakha is not like him. But Rabbeinu Tam and Rabbi Yitzchak explained that the halakha is like Rabbi Natan, for regarding the dispute of Abaye and Rava in the chapter “Kol Sha’a” (Pesachim 31a), where Rava said that [the creditor] collects from now onward, it is impossible for Rava to resolve [the matter] according to Rav Nachman — who said that if orphans collected land for their father’s debt, the creditor returns and collects it from them — except [by following] Rabbi Natan. And we rule like Rav Nachman in monetary law, and Rava too strained to establish it as he did, and we rule like Rava in disputes with Abaye. As for what I brought — that since the halakha is not like Rabbi Eliezer regarding the master giving him a Canaanite maidservant, let us likewise say that the halakha is not like him regarding the severance gift — this is no proof, for perhaps the halakha is not like him on that point, but on others the halakha is like him. Furthermore, perhaps even regarding one who sells himself, the halakha is like him that the master gives him a Canaanite maidservant, and the phrase “go steal” was used there for the sake of elegance, since if the court sold him, everyone agrees that the master gives him a Canaanite maidservant. And as for what is said that Rabbi Eliezer is a Shammaite — in most books the reading is Rabbi Elazar. And as for what [the Gemara] says, “It is Tutai’s” — perhaps it means: it is Tutai’s, and he holds like him. And Rabbeinu Natanel explains: regarding a loan, everyone holds like Rabbi Natan, and so we explain above according to Rabbi Eliezer: Rather, [the verse] “to him and not to his creditor” — because we generally hold like Rabbi Natan in other hiring cases, where one takes from this person and gives to that one, the word “to him” comes and excludes it. That is, he does not pay the severance gift to the creditor. “And the other,” the first *tanna*, [holds] “in general too” — that is, in other hiring cases we do not rule like Rabbi Natan, because [the worker] labors with his body; but regarding a creditor, everyone holds like Rabbi Natan, as I explained.
